subject: DPA: role delegation clarifications + SCCs mapping for Order Form
messages:
From: Elena Martin <elena.martin@sunrisehealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@sunrisehealth.com, tom.reyes@sunrisehealth.com
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 09:12:14 +0200
Subject: Sunrise - DPA redlines & SCCs mapping for order form

Hi Laura / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, attaching our redlines to the proposed DPA and an annotated order form (attachments below). High-level asks from our side:

- We need clearer role delegation language in Section 2 (processor vs controller) for the analytics feature (customer PII used for model feedback).
- We require explicit SCC modules called out for transfers to the US and an option for a Transfer Impact Addendum if needed.
- Please confirm the list of subprocessors and any planned changes (we cannot accept a fully open-ended subprocessor clause).

Could we get an internal read by end of week? If helpful, we can do a short legal-to-legal call on Wednesday morning (CEST).

Attachments:
- Sunrise_DPA_redlines.docx (docx)
- OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Elena Martin
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Sunrise Health
elena.martin@sunrisehealth.com
+44 20 7946 0123
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 11:03:02 +0200
Subject: Re: Sunrise - DPA redlines & SCCs mapping for order form

Elena —

Thanks for sending these over and for the clear summary. We've started an internal review and I pulled in Karthis (privacy) and Irene (legal ops) to coordinate evidence. High-level responses below; detailed redline doc (RWD_DPA_response_v1.docx) attached.

Immediate notes:
1) Roles: we agree to clarify analytics flows. We'll propose language that narrows "processor" functions for analytics to exclude identity-resolution steps unless explicitly enabled in the Order Form.
2) SCCs: we'll map the SCC modules that apply for EU->US transfers and include language that allows a Transfer Impact Addendum for particularly sensitive datasets.
3) Subprocessors: we can provide an explicit initial list and commit to 30 days' notice for additions; we cannot accept a full prohibition on future subprocessors.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal: Karthis to produce a proposed clause set for Section 2 and the SCC module table by EOD Wednesday (26 Jun).
- Legal-to-legal call: Elena, you suggested Wed morning CEST — Ben will propose a time.
- Evidence: Irene to confirm what materials we can share (SOC2 summary, KMS attestations, subprocessor list).

Can you flag any non-starters (e.g., strict data localization for the analytics pipeline) before the call?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
VP Legal — Contracts
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: RWD_DPA_response_v1.docx

Laura / Ben — thanks, 09:00 CEST on Wed works. A few clarifications ahead of the call (so we can be efficient):

- Data localization: For our mental-health subset we will require that raw audio and transcripts remain in EU region storage and processing unless we sign a Transfer Impact Addendum. That is a hard requirement for those datasets.

- Subprocessors: we can accept a 30-day notice for additions only if there is a clear mechanism for objection and the ability to require an alternative arrangement. We cannot accept blanket acceptance without an objection path.

- Evidence: please bring SOC2 Type II scope, a short KMS/HSM architecture diagram, and the current subprocessor roster.

I will circulate a short internal checklist prior to the call so we can tag must-haves vs negotiables.

On Wed — Elena

Elena — thanks again for the call this morning and for the checklist you shared. Summarizing agreed next steps and the internal asks so nothing gets lost: 

Agreed (high level):
- For the mental-health dataset we will gate cross-border processing pending a signed Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA). Redwood will not process raw audio/transcripts outside EU for that dataset unless the TIA is executed.
- We will provide an initial subprocessor roster (see attached) and commit to 30 days' notice for additions; addition notices will include a right to object and require good-faith efforts to find an alternative arrangement.
- SCCs: Redwood will reference the standard EU SCCs and include an SCCs mapping table in the Order Form annex. A TIA template will be provided if Sunrise requests it.

Internal asks for Redwood Legal/Ops (action owners):
- Karthis (karthik_iyer): finalize proposed Section 2 redline and SCCs mapping table by Tue 2 Jul 2028.
- Irene (irene_choi): pull SOC2 Type II scope, KMS attestation doc, and current subprocessor roster by Mon 1 Jul 2028.
- Contracts / Sales (ben_carter): confirm whether the mental-health dataset will be a separate line-item in the Order Form or managed via a data handling addendum.

Links / artifacts:
- Drive folder (redwood): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/0B_RAD_sample_dpa_responses
- HubSpot deal: RDW-2028-1482
- Draft TIA template: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/TIA-template-2028

Irene / Karthis — please confirm timelines and flag any non-starters. Elena — if you can share the mental-health dataset scoping doc we discussed (approx. data types/volumes) that will help us scope a TIA.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
VP Legal — Contracts
Redwood Inference
